knowledge_gaps: The model-high-score panel has a structural limitation: selecting the same model’s top 32 alternatives makes the target’s panel rank equal to its full-catalog rank capped at 33, under consistent tie handling. Its outranking fraction saturates at 1 once at least 32 alternatives beat the target. Report this as a censored catalog-ranking diagnostic; greater difficulty is guaranteed by construction and does not independently reveal a failure mechanism.

Equal panel sizes do not isolate candidate difficulty. Panels also differ in popularity, semantic similarity, missing-text coverage and eligible rows. Report paired contrasts on rows where all compared panels are available, alongside panel-specific coverage and candidate characteristics.

Reproducibility requires explicit frequency-bin boundaries and tie rules, interaction-count versus user-count frequency, TF-IDF preprocessing and vocabulary settings, zero-similarity handling, catalog-ID mapping, row-sampling rules, history-length strata and score-tie conventions. The pseudocode also needs explicit B × L × D feature indexing and B × 1 × K candidate shapes.

Training-positive ranking remains vulnerable to memorization and repeated-item shortcuts. Record whether targets already occur in their visible prefixes and report repeat-target versus novel-target strata. Neither strong nor weak training-panel results establish generalization or justify changing training.

The supplied workflow describes an unperturbed diagnosis module, whereas earlier results describe implemented perturbations and a backbone audit. Establish which code and checkpoint produced each result before treating those measurements as evidence for the current implementation.

The proposal changes a previously declared follow-up sequence without explaining the amendment. Predeclare the revised diagnostic scope and a computation cap; 128 rows alone does not bound full-catalog scoring time.

Originality 4/10 is reasonable. Potential 7/10 is optimistic without evidence that these diagnostics guide validation improvements; approximately 5–6/10 is better supported. Difficulty 3/10 may underestimate adapter verification, sparse text retrieval, catalog scoring and missingness handling; approximately 4–5/10 is more credible. No additional independently trained predictor is needed.

follow_up_queries.reason: Clarify which panel statistics contain useful ranking information and which are consequences of selecting candidates with the evaluated model itself.
follow_up_queries.query: In recommender-system diagnostics, when alternatives are the evaluated model's own top-K items, how does ranking a positive against those alternatives relate to its censored full-catalog rank? What limitations do hard-negative selection, score ties and saturation impose when comparing this panel with uniform negative sampling?

follow_up_queries.reason: Find defensible controls for comparing candidate constructions when missing text, popularity and eligibility differ.
follow_up_queries.query: What methodological controls are recommended for paired comparisons of uniform, popularity-matched, TF-IDF-neighbor and model-mined candidate panels in sequential recommendation, especially common-row eligibility, missing metadata, candidate overlap, popularity confounding and repeated training histories?

follow_up_queries.reason: Determine how to detect training-history shortcuts without claiming that training diagnostics measure held-out performance.
follow_up_queries.query: What research distinguishes memorization and repeat-item shortcuts from generalization in sequential recommendation, and how should training-positive ranking diagnostics be stratified by target occurrence in the input prefix, item frequency and history length while preserving a separate fixed validation evaluator?
